intro: Convert millimeters (mm) to meters (m) instantly for architectural drawings, carpentry cut lists, CNC machining tolerances, and physics problems. Under the SI metric system, 1 meter equals exactly 1,000 millimeters—so 1 mm equals 0.001 m (1 × 10⁻³ m in scientific notation). Simply divide millimeters by 1,000 by shifting the decimal three places left, or check values from 0.005 mm to 30,000 mm below.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Decimal Shift (÷1,000 vs. ÷100) & Length mm vs. Chemistry mM
items: Move the decimal point three places left (÷ 1,000) when converting millimeters to meters—not two places left (which converts centimeters to meters). For example, 60 mm is 0.06 m, not 0.6 m.
Lowercase 'mm' means millimeter (length, 10⁻³ m), whereas 'mM' in chemistry stands for millimolar concentration (10⁻³ mol/L = 0.001 M)—the two units measure completely different physical quantities.

faqs.question: How many meters are in 1 millimeter?
faqs.answer: There are exactly 0.001 meters in 1 millimeter (1/1,000 m). Conversely, 1 meter contains exactly 1,000 millimeters.

faqs.question: How do you write mm to m in scientific notation?
faqs.answer: Multiply millimeters by 10⁻³ to get meters: 1 mm = 1 × 10⁻³ m. For example, 0.15 mm = 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ m, and 30,000 mm = 3 × 10¹ m (30 m).

faqs.question: How do I convert millimeters to meters mentally?
faqs.answer: Shift the decimal point three places to the left (divide by 1,000). For example, 876 mm becomes 0.876 m, and 1,150 mm becomes 1.15 m.
